subject.title: Feature: Message continuation marker for batched input (cost savings)

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit user-authored continuation marker, or should timer/adaptive inbound aggregation remain the only supported pre-run batching model?
rationale: These approaches create different public message semantics, configuration, timeout behavior, and cross-channel expectations, so implementation evidence cannot safely choose between them.

options.title: Add generic marker mode
options.body: Approve an opt-in shared aggregation mode with configurable marker and timeout, marker stripping, command and media bypass, and focused contract tests.

options.title: Keep timer-only batching
options.body: Treat the existing inbound debounce mechanism as the supported product answer and document that explicit continuation markers are not planned.

options.title: Unify aggregation designs
options.body: First define one broader contract covering markers, adaptive timing, and semantic aggregation before adding new public configuration.

recommendation.title: Add generic marker mode
recommendation.body: Approve an opt-in shared aggregation mode with configurable marker and timeout, marker stripping, command and media bypass, and focused contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They previously reviewed this exact choice and have the strongest adjacent shared inbound and queue history in the available evidence.
